method: Diff-scoped round: the 39 sentences gate scope listed since round 1, plus chart text changed by code alone, the changed gate.toml entries, docs/sources.json's ref, amendment A5, the references-data.md changes and the five rewritten reference entries (65 items). findings.claim: I worked on a payroll in Indonesia, and under Indonesian law a share of that pay should have gone into an old-age savings account: Jaminan Hari Tua, or JHT, run by BPJS Ketenagakerjaan.
findings.evidence: L: Draft line 5. The wording is the one the owner approved after round 1, recorded in design doc line 140 (A5): 'should have gone into'. The legal duty is real. PP 46/2015 Pasal 2(2) (sources/text/pp_46_2015.txt:122) says 'Setiap orang yang bekerja wajib mendaftarkan dirinya dalam program JHT'. Pasal 16(1) (line 428) sets 2% from the worker and 3.7% from the employer, and Pasal 19(1) (lines 505-508) requires the employer to pay it in. The duty applies only to a non-state employer that has been phased in: Pasal 2(1) at lines 116-121 says 'sesuai penahapan kepesertaan', and Pasal 3 at line 133 leaves state employers to a separate regulation. The owner's facts do not name his employer or the dates. His own wording ('was not aware of the BPJS Ketenagakerjaan deduction') presents the deduction as one that applied to that payroll, and the sentence rests on that. In round 1 my lens noted the same dependence on the employer having been phased in (round1-verdicts.json r1:item:18, lens L). The narrowing to 'should have gone into' addressed whether money was actually deducted, but not this condition. | H: Personal part: the owner said he worked on a payroll in Indonesia, was not aware of the BPJS Ketenagakerjaan deduction, and does not know whether anything was deducted. 'should have gone into' matches all three and goes no further. Legal part: PP 46/2015 Pasal 2(2) says every person who works must register in JHT (sources/text/pp_46_2015.txt:120-123), and Pasal 16(1) puts 2% of wages on the worker (pp_46_2015.txt:428-434). What a hostile Indonesian worker can raise: Pasal 2(1) phases employers in ('sesuai penahapan kepesertaan', :118-121), and Pasal 3 and Pasal 4(1)a leave state employers out (:131-142). Nothing on file says what kind of employer he had or when; the owner's phrase 'the deduction' assumes his job was covered (r1:item:371 note). Against the title: there is no contradiction under round 1's ruling that the title states a legal duty (r1:item:1, PP 46 Pasal 2(2)). Still, 'should have gone into' can be read as 'but it did not', so the title's 'Forced to Save' now holds only as that legal duty (see extra on the title). Against 'It is how a worker can pay into such an account, year after year, without noticing' (draft line 5): that sentence is about 'a worker' and says 'can', so it states a general possibility, not the author's case (r1:item:11). The narrowing only means his own case is no longer offered as a confirmed example. Owner decision of 2026-10-23 (design A5, inventory [56]) keeps the wording.

findings.claim: A separate pension scheme, Jaminan Pensiun, takes another 3 percent (Pemerintah Republik Indonesia, 2015a); it pays a pension, so I leave it out of the growth comparison.
findings.evidence: S: sources/text/pp_45_2015.txt lines 820-825 (Pasal 28(2)): 'Iuran ... sebesar 3% (tiga persen) dari Upah per bulan'. Lines 60-64 (Pasal 1(3)): 'Manfaat Pensiun adalah sejumlah uang yang dibayarkan setiap bulan', and Pasal 16 (lines 457-466) lists the pension benefits. So 'it pays a pension' holds. Deleting 'rather than building a balance' removed the conflict with Pasal 24(1) (lines 737-742, the lump sum for members with under 15 years). The 'so I leave it out' logic still rests on the scheme being a pension. Not introduced by round 1: Pasal 29(2) (lines 855-858) caps the wage base, so for pay above the ceiling the scheme takes less than 3 percent of pay. The sentence follows the regulation's own '3% dari Upah per bulan'.

findings.claim: The window stops in 2020 for a reason I come back to: BPJS has not published the rate it credited to balances since.
findings.evidence: L: Draft line 32. The bare 'since' points back to the '2020' earlier in the same sentence ('The window stops in 2020'), so the reader takes 2020 as a rate year. Read that way, results.json published.years_without_credited is 2021 to 2025 (n=5), and the sentence is true under both readings of 2020's 5.59%. If 5.59% is the credited rate, it was published and nothing came after. If it is not, nothing has been published for 2021 onward either. One residual problem: under the second reading, 'not since 2020' still implies that 2020's rate was published. The limits bullet at line 77 and the notes on charts 1, 2 and 4 cancel that by calling 2020 an inference. A second reading also fails. Read 'since' as a publication date, and the sentence is false under either reading. BPJS's 2019 report, which gives 6.08% credited for 2019, is cited in the post as (2021a) and was listed on the BPJS page only by Feb 2021 (references-data.md). The 2020 summary that prints 5.59% (sources/provenance/jht/lk_lpp_2020_summary.pdf) is dated 'Jakarta, 31 Mei 2021'. Line 77 ('BPJS has not published the credited rate since.') uses the same construction.
findings.fix: H extra E1b: 'has not published ... since' reads as publication time, and BPJS published the 2019 rate in February 2021 (2021a). Narrowed to 'for later years'.

findings.claim: The money must go in by law, from the worker and the employer.
findings.evidence: L: Draft line 68. This is a claim about the duty to contribute, not about who is covered. PP 46 Pasal 16(1) (pp_46_2015.txt:428) sets 2% from the worker and 3.7% from the employer, and Pasal 19(1) (lines 505-508) says the employer 'wajib menyetor Iuran JHT'. Round 1 refuted r1:item:18 ('JHT is compulsory for wage earners') because Pasal 2(1) phases employers in and Pasal 3 leaves state employers out. That was a claim that every wage earner is in JHT, which this sentence does not make. The paragraph still argues validly: the second sentence works as the unstated reason for 'Indonesia does not need a 401(k)', and 'that money' in the third sentence refers back to it. Two weaknesses remain, both left by deleting 'It already does the hard part:'. 'The money' now has no antecedent in its section and has to be picked up from line 13. And the employer share applies only to wage-earner members; non-wage-earner members pay alone under Pasal 18 and 21. | H: 'must go in by law' states a duty, not an outcome: PP 46/2015 Pasal 16(1) sets 5.7% of wages, 2% borne by the worker and 3.7% by the employer (pp_46_2015.txt:428-434), and Pasal 2(2) sets the duty to register (:120-123). BPJS's own 2022 report on non-compliant employers ('belum patuh', bpjs_ir_2022.txt:14254-14262) therefore does not refute it, which is why round 1 changed 'goes in' to 'must go in' (r1:item:76). Scope notes: the worker-and-employer split applies to wage earners at non-state employers (the Pasal 16(1) text); non-wage members pay alone. The paragraph is about wage earners. 'The money' has no antecedent inside the paragraph, but it had none before round 1 either (round 1 snapshot line 68: 'the money goes in by law').

findings.claim: What Indonesia does not do is make that money feel like yours.
findings.evidence: H: This is opinion in the lessons section; round 1 kept the earlier form as opinion (r1:item:77). Replacing 'it' with 'Indonesia' keeps the same referent: in the round 1 snapshot (draft line 68) 'It already does the hard part... What it does not do' already pointed to 'Indonesia'. A hostile BPJS official can quote the post against it. Line 17 says the law makes BPJS tell members their balance and its growth once a year (PP 46 Pasal 22(7), pp_46_2015.txt:604-607), and line 62 gives JMO's 33,682,397 registered users. The deleted contrast ('JHT leaves more of the looking to the member') used to support the sentence. What is left: the unpublished credited rate (results.json published.years_without_credited = 2021 to 2025), the 2022 report's low brand awareness (line 64), and the owner's own unawareness. That is enough for a stated opinion.

findings.claim: Publish the rate credited to balances each year.
findings.evidence: L: Draft line 70. This is a policy suggestion addressed to BPJS, not financial advice. It follows from line 62, where the credited rate has not been published for 2021 to 2025. After two lessons were removed, two remain: publishing the rate and showing the payslip line. So the plural in 'The lessons I take from the 401(k) are small and practical' still holds, and 'This would not change how JHT is invested' is still true of both, since both are about disclosure. One link is weaker than before. The connection to the 401(k) now rests on the owner's own view stated before any data (line 7, 'watch your money grow') rather than on the deleted statement contrast. That is acceptable for 'The lessons I take'. | H: The recommendation assumes the rate is not published, and the post's evidence supports that: results.json published.years_without_credited = [2021..2025], plus the gap search over the BPJS news archive and the 2022 to 2025 summaries (r1:item:70, r1:item:331). A yearly rate still exists to publish: Peraturan BPJS 3/2020 Pasal 2(6) and Pasal 5(1) set a 'Tingkat Pengembangan tahunan' and credit it every 1 January (docs/provenance-audit.md, Pasal 2(6) and 5(1) entries). The sentence is aimed at BPJS, so it is policy, not financial advice. Note for a US retirement economist: after the statement lesson was deleted, 'lessons I take from the 401(k)' ties to this lesson only through the thesis, since a 401(k) declares no single crediting rate (balances are valued at market). The sentence never says a 401(k) does this, so it stays opinion.
